newsitem.title: USA: Ford shares fall on Latam concerns - traders.
newsitem.headline: Ford shares fall on Latam concerns - traders.

text.p: Shares of Ford Motor Co dropped in mid-morning action on concerns over weakness in operations in Brazil and Argentina, traders said.

Bear Stearns analyst Nicholas Lobaccaro was considering a cut in his Ford second-half earnings estimate, possibly to $1.65 per share from the current $1.90, pending a discussion with management, according to a Bear Stearns source.

Lobaccaro cited a Securities and Exchange Commission filing late Monday in which Ford said its expected performance in Brazil in the second half would be substantially worse than the first-half performance, according to the source.
Lobaccaro said that the development could delay the automaker's earnings recovery and expose weakness in its international operations, according to the source.
The analyst maintained an attractive rating on the shares, according to the source.
On August 27, Ford announced that James Padilla will replace Gurminder Bedi as president of Ford Brazil and Argentina, effective November 1.
Padilla is currently vehicle line director for performance luxury at Vehicle Center 3, a Dearborn, Mich.-based unit that develops rear-wheel drive cars, the company said.
With the transfer, he will be located in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and report to Ed Hagenlocker, president of Ford automotive operations.
